description: Public frontend (Public/frontend-v6): surface the real reason for a failed chat instead of masking every non-ok response with the generic 'Sorry, something went wrong' error. When the server returns HTTP 503 (usage/budget limit or busy) or 429 (per-IP rate limit), show a DISTINCT friendly bilingual message; keep the existing generic 502/network fallback. Do NOT change the send/timeout/linkify logic from PR#406 — links must still render. This feature is independent of FEAT-002 and could be parallelized.
steps: In Public/frontend-v6/src/lib/i18n.ts, add two new keys to BOTH the en and hi objects (near chat_error/chat_welcome): `chat_limit` (503/usage-limit message, e.g. en: 'The assistant has reached today’s limit or is busy. Please try again shortly.' / hi Devanagari equivalent), and `chat_busy` (429/rate-limit 'please wait a moment' message, e.g. en: 'You’re sending messages too fast. Please wait a moment and try again.' / hi equivalent). Keep chat_error unchanged for the generic 502/network case. Match the existing key style and both locales must have identical key sets (there may be an existing test asserting en/hi parity — keep it green).

In Public/frontend-v6/src/lib/components/Chatbot.svelte send(), after `const data = await res.json().catch(() => null)`, branch on the response: if res.ok && data.ok && data.answer -> render the answer (unchanged). Else choose the error text by status: for res.status === 503 use the server's `data.error` string when present, else $tr('chat_limit'); for res.status === 429 use `data.error` when present, else $tr('chat_busy'); for everything else (502, other, or thrown/network) use $tr('chat_error'). Keep the catch{} network branch showing $tr('chat_error'). Preserve the AbortController/CHAT_TIMEOUT_MS timeout logic and the linkifyTokens rendering exactly as they are.
Do NOT modify the transcript rendering block (linkifyTokens / anchor markup) — it must keep working so PR#406 links still render.

Add/extend a Chatbot component test. Create Public/frontend-v6/src/lib/components/Chatbot.status.test.ts (vitest + jsdom, following the mount/unmount/flushSync pattern in Chatbot.linkify.test.ts). Since send() calls fetch, stub global.fetch (vi.stubGlobal or vi.fn) to return a Response-like object with a given status/ok and json(). Tests: (1) a 503 response (ok:false, status:503, body {ok:false,error:'...limit...'}) renders a limit message DISTINCT from the generic chat_error text — assert the transcript contains the server error text (or the chat_limit string) and NOT the chat_error string; (2) a 200 response whose answer contains a URL still renders a clickable <a> anchor (regression guard for PR#406). Drive send() by typing into the input and clicking Send (or dispatching Enter), then flushSync and await microtasks so the fetch promise resolves.

Run `cd Public/frontend-v6 && npm run check` (0/0), `npm test` (all pass incl. new tests), and `npm run build`. Confirm the client JS size stays under the CI budget of 700000 bytes (baseline ~638,706 B; three short i18n strings + a small branch add negligible size).
acceptance_criteria: i18n.ts has chat_limit and chat_busy in both en and hi with matching key sets; chat_error unchanged.
Chatbot.svelte shows a distinct message for 503 (limit/busy) and 429 (rate) using the server error string when present, and keeps chat_error for 502/network.
The PR#406 linkify/anchor rendering and the PR#406 send/timeout logic are unchanged and still work.
New Chatbot.status.test.ts proves a 503 renders a limit message distinct from the generic chat_error, and a 200 with a link still renders an anchor.
`npm run check` is 0/0, `npm test` all pass, `npm run build` succeeds, and total client JS stays <= 700000 bytes.
verification: Run `cd Public/frontend-v6 && npm run check && npm test && npm run build` and confirm 0 errors, all tests pass, build succeeds.
After build, compute total client JS bytes (as the CI job does) and confirm <= 700000.
findings: Implemented frontend-only fix in Public/frontend-v6. Changes: (1) src/lib/i18n.ts — added two keys `chat_limit` and `chat_busy` to BOTH the en and hi objects (the spec's 'three keys' phrasing was inconsistent; the steps/acceptance criteria name exactly chat_limit + chat_busy, so two keys were added). en: chat_limit='The assistant has reached today’s limit or is busy right now. Please try again shortly.', chat_busy='You’re sending messages too fast. Please wait a moment and try again.'; hi given natural Devanagari equivalents matching the existing chat_error/chat_welcome tone. chat_error left unchanged; both locales keep identical key sets. (2) src/lib/components/Chatbot.svelte send() failure branch now selects the message by HTTP status: 503 -> data.error when present else $tr('chat_limit'); 429 -> data.error when present else $tr('chat_busy'); everything else (502/other) -> $tr('chat_error'); catch{} network branch still $tr('chat_error'). The success branch, AbortController/CHAT_TIMEOUT_MS timeout logic, and linkifyTokens transcript rendering (PR#406) were left exactly as-is. (3) Added src/lib/components/Chatbot.status.test.ts (vitest+jsdom, mount/unmount/flushSync pattern) stubbing global fetch: test 1 asserts a 503 surfaces the server error text (or chat_limit) and NOT chat_error; test 2 is a PR#406 regression guard asserting a 200 answer with a <https://...> URL still renders a clickable <a target=_blank rel~=noopener> anchor. Note: driving send() needed a macrotask flush loop (setTimeout(0) + flushSync x5) because send() awaits fetch() then res.json() then a state update; a few microtask ticks alone were not enough. VERIFICATION (node v22.23.2): `npm run check` = 0 errors / 0 warnings; `npm test` = 311 passed / 0 failed (baseline 309 + 2 new), 19 test files; `npm run build` succeeds. Client JS budget: total client JS = 624833 bytes (CI limit 700000, well under; note this is slightly below the quoted ~638,706 B baseline). Per-page first-load worst = 370863 bytes (CI limit 420000, passes). No branch/commit/push performed per instructions.
